faqs.a: Upload the photo and raise the amount slider from 0 to 3. Values around 0.8–1.2 suit most photos; higher values give a punchy, edgy look. Press Download to save.
faqs.q: How do I sharpen a blurry photo?

faqs.a: It uses unsharp masking: a blurred copy is subtracted from the original to find edges, then those edges are amplified by your amount setting.
Honestly: no. Sharpening enhances edges that are already there; it cannot recreate detail lost to bad focus or motion blur. Expect crisper, not miraculous.
faqs.q: Can it fix a very blurry photo?

faqs.a: Usually yes — most phone photos benefit from a light 0.5–1.0 sharpen. But noisy night shots can look worse, because sharpening also amplifies grain.
Pushing the amount past about 2 creates bright/dark halos along edges and crunchy noise. If you see halos, dial it back.
faqs.q: Why do I see halos around edges?

faqs.a: No. Everything is computed pixel-by-pixel in your browser; the photo is never uploaded anywhere.

sharpen-image.formula:
blur = gaussian_blur(image, 1px)
out = original + amount × (original − blur)
amount 0–3, result clamped to 0–255
howTo: Upload the photo you want to sharpen.
Raise the amount slider slowly and watch edges crisp up in the preview.
Stop before halos appear — around 1.0 for most photos.
Choose PNG or JPG output format.
Press Download to save the sharpened image.
keyFacts: Unsharp masking compares each pixel with a blurred copy to find edges.
The difference (original − blur) is added back, scaled by your amount setting.
Amount 0 means no change; amount 3 is very aggressive.
The result is clamped to 0–255 so no channel can overflow.
Sharpening works at full resolution — no pixels are added or removed.

sharpen-image.workedExample:
A pixel with original value 120 and blurred value 100, amount 1.5:
out = 120 + 1.5 × (120 − 100) = 120 + 30 = 150
The edge pixel brightens from 120 to 150, increasing local contrast. A flat-area pixel (120 vs blurred 118) barely moves: 120 + 1.5 × 2 = 123.
